course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
unit.description: Compare additive and multiplicative change, then build, compose, invert, and model with exponential and logarithmic functions, including residuals and semi-log plots.

quiz.title: Unit 2 FRQ 1: Function concepts (Topics 2.1 to 2.8)
quiz.headline: Composition and inverse values, a zero and end behavior of an exponential function, and choosing a function type from a table.
quiz.promptTitle: Free response 1 · Function concepts · graphing calculator
quiz.prompt: The function f is given by f(x) = 3(2)ˣ − 12. The table gives values of a function g at selected values of x.
quiz.instructions: Part A style: a graphing calculator is required. Show the work that leads to each answer; answers without supporting work may not earn credit where work is requested. Avoid rounding intermediate values, and give decimal approximations accurate to three places after the decimal point unless the part says otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, the domain of a function f is the set of all real numbers x for which f(x) is a real number.
quiz.note: Original practice question written in the AP Precalculus free-response format (6 points, parts A to C). Scoring is self-assessed with the point-by-point rubric. It is not an official AP question or an official AP score.

scaffold.label: Show work
scaffold.text: Write the setup, such as the expression you evaluate or the equation you solve, before the answer.

scaffold.label: Use notation
scaffold.text: Use limit notation, interval notation, and units exactly where a part asks for them.

scaffold.label: Justify
scaffold.text: When a part says give a reason or explain, refer to the given values or the context.

responseFields.label: Part A (i)
responseFields.prompt: A (i). Find the value of g(f(3)) as an exact value. Show the work that leads to your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part A (ii)
responseFields.prompt: A (ii). The function f is invertible. Find the value of f⁻¹(36). Show the work that leads to your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (i)
responseFields.prompt: B (i). Find all real zeros of f.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (ii)
responseFields.prompt: B (ii). Determine the end behavior of f as x decreases without bound. Express your answer using the mathematical notation of a limit.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (i)
responseFields.prompt: C (i). Based on the table, determine which of the following function types best models g: linear, quadratic, or exponential.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (ii)
responseFields.prompt: C (ii). Give a reason for your answer to part C (i) based on the relationship between the change in the output values of g and the change in the input values of g. Refer to the values in the table in your reasoning.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

rubric.label: A (i) Composite value
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for g(f(3)) = g(12) = −3, with f(3) = 3(8) − 12 = 12 shown.

rubric.label: A (ii) Inverse value
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for f⁻¹(36) = 4, with work such as 3(2)ˣ − 12 = 36, 2ˣ = 16, x = 4, or the reasoning that f(4) = 36.

rubric.label: B (i) Real zero
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for x = 2, from 3(2)ˣ = 12 and 2ˣ = 4.

rubric.label: B (ii) End behavior with limit notation
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for lim x→−∞ f(x) = −12. A description without limit notation does not earn the point.

rubric.label: C (i) Function type
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: g is best modeled by a linear function.

rubric.label: C (ii) Reason
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: over consecutive equal-length input-value intervals of length 4, the output values of g change by a constant −4, so g changes at a constant rate.

quiz.modelResponse:
A (i). f(3) = 3(2)³ − 12 = 24 − 12 = 12. Then g(f(3)) = g(12) = −3.

A (ii). f(x) = 36 gives 3(2)ˣ − 12 = 36, so 3(2)ˣ = 48, 2ˣ = 16, and x = 4. Since f(4) = 36, f⁻¹(36) = 4.

B (i). f(x) = 0 gives 3(2)ˣ = 12, so 2ˣ = 4 and x = 2. The only real zero of f is x = 2.

B (ii). As x decreases without bound, 2ˣ gets arbitrarily close to 0, so 3(2)ˣ − 12 gets arbitrarily close to −12: lim x→−∞ f(x) = −12.

C (i). g is best modeled by a linear function.

C (ii). The input values increase by 4 each time, and the output values change by 5 − 9 = −4, 1 − 5 = −4, −3 − 1 = −4, and −7 − (−3) = −4. Because the output values change by a constant amount over consecutive equal-length input-value intervals, g changes at a constant rate, which is the behavior of a linear function.
quiz.alternateModel: In A (ii) it is enough to observe from f(4) = 3(16) − 12 = 36 that f⁻¹(36) = 4. In C (ii) you may also note that the ratios 5/9, 1/5, −3/1 are not constant, which rules out an exponential model.
commonErrors: Computing f(g(3)), the composition in the other order.
Giving f⁻¹(36) as 1/f(36) or as f(36).
Writing lim x→−∞ f(x) = 0, forgetting the −12 translation.
Choosing exponential because the outputs decrease.
Giving differences without saying the input intervals have equal length.
